newsitem.title: USA: U.S. urges return to calm in Northern Ireland.
newsitem.headline: U.S. urges return to calm in Northern Ireland.

text.p: The United States said on Monday it was deeply concerned by the weekend violence in Northern Ireland and urged Protestants and Catholics to return to "calm and constructive efforts" to reinvigorate peace talks.
State Department spokesman Nicholas Burns, however, did not criticise authorities for allowing the Protestant parade through a Catholic area of Portadown that sparked the unrest.
"We are not going to second guess the decision of the British authorities and the Royal Ulster Constabulary (RUC) to allow the parade. That decision was made on security grounds," he said.
Burns added that in making the decision, they perhaps had hoped to limit violence.

"The United States was deeply concerned, deeply saddened by the confrontations ...it's very regrettable that efforts to work out mutually acceptable arrangements between Catholic leaders and Protestant leaders for the handling of the Portadown march, that those negotiations failed," he said.
Burns said the task of reconciliation now fell even more heavily on the leaders of the Protestant and Catholic communities.
"The United States urges a return to calm and constructive efforts to invigorate the multiparty talks, which still, we believe, offer the best hope for peace in Northern Ireland," he said.

The outbreak of nationalist unrest was the worst in years, in which rioters and police clashed in Belfast, Londonderry and other towns after the Protestant Orange Order march was allowed through a Catholic area.
